fields.why: The only contrast is pairwise SNP distances classified against a 10-SNP relatedness cutpoint ('Only two out of seven serotype 4 isolates were highly genomically related'), which reads more as quantization feeding a count than as an outcome compared with a target. B's 'comparison' follows the brief's literal 'threshold' wording, so both are defensible.

Same case: B's 'fixed referent' (10 SNPs) is defensible under the brief's wording; A gives 'none' but its own notes call the 10-SNP threshold 'the fixed referent', which is inconsistent. Rule needed: a laboratory cutpoint used to classify units (relatedness, positivity) is quantization, not a fixed-referent comparison.

brief_issues: The brief lists 'a threshold' as a fixed referent but also treats cutpoints as quantization; it should say whether a classification cutpoint (e.g., a 10-SNP relatedness rule) makes a comparison. Also unclear whether a dose count from an outbreak-response clinic (87 PCV20 doses) counts as coverage/uptake.
